description: Hierarchical prompt tree for implementing the multi-layer, generative, CNF-cross-referenced, reflective geometric-spectral framework in Rust. Concrete CNF problems emitted by the Rust implementation may be collapsed by Cadical. This version adds an explicit Flag-6 subtree that expresses the terminal infinite-lift problem in CNF terms and generates the corresponding Rust scaffolding. Flag 6 itself remains an analytic open problem; the CNF/SAT layer only supplies the finite approximations and the hooks for the required lifts.
collapse_rule: The multi-layer generative framework does not collapse its residual difficulty onto a single classical open problem before generating concrete CNF instances. Once Rust has emitted a concrete CNF formula, that output problem is permitted to be collapsed to a solution by Cadical. The infinite lift (Flag 6) cannot be performed by SAT alone and remains conditional on analytic flags (tightness, uniform Mourre, continuity of residual extraction, Lyapunov functional).

root.title: Geometric-Spectral Framework in Rust
root.prompt: Implement a modular Rust crate that realises the geometric-spectral framework as an open multi-layer, generative, CNF-cross-referenced and reflective system. Fully support the parameterized family Φ_{N,M,K} and provide scaffolding for the Flag-6 infinite lift. The SAT layer decides only finite instances; the infinite statement is external.

children.title: Parameterized Φ (existing)
children.prompt: Retain the full parameterized Φ_{N,M,K} emission, Cadical integration, and model examination already present in the tree.

children.title: Flag 6 — Infinite Zero-Set Lift expressed in CNF + Rust
children.prompt:
Flag 6 (terminal): Prove that residual continuous spectrum vanishes for a limiting spectral measure whose pure-point support is exactly the set of all non-trivial zeros of Ξ.

Express this flag in CNF terms as the following limiting statement about the family of finite formulae:

  For every finite K there exists a model of Φ^⋆_{N,M,K} (with N,M sufficiently large relative to K) in which the first K zeros are realised and residual mass is zero once the reflective fixpoint is reached;
  AND the family of residual densities of those models is tight;
  AND every weak-* limit point has residual mass identically zero and pure-point support exactly the non-trivial zeros of Ξ.

The first conjunct is decided by Cadical on finite CNF instances. The second and third conjuncts are analytic and cannot be expressed as a single finite CNF formula. The Rust implementation must therefore:
1. emit and solve the finite CNF family,
2. extract residual densities and pure-point locations from the models,
3. expose clear extension points (traits / hooks) where a future tightness proof, Mourre estimate, continuity proof for T, or Lyapunov functional can be attached,
4. never claim that SAT has solved Flag 6.

Generate the Rust modules described in the children below.

children.title: CNF Family Emitter for Flag 6
children.prompt: Implement a Rust type Flag6CnfFamily that, given bounds (N_max, M_max, K_max), systematically emits the sequence of CnfFormulae Φ^⋆_{N,M,K} for all 1 ≤ N ≤ N_max, 1 ≤ M ≤ M_max, 1 ≤ K ≤ K_max (or a configurable subset). Each formula must be independently solvable by Cadical. Provide a method that runs Cadical on the whole family and collects a structured report: for each (N,M,K) the SAT/UNSAT status, whether residual vanished, and the realised pure-point locations. This report is the propositional shadow of Flag 6; the infinite lift is not performed here.

children.title: Model Extraction and Residual Density Recording
children.prompt:
From every SAT model returned by Cadical, extract:
- the set of realised Z_k,
- the residual vector (R_{i,d}) at every depth,
- the final residual mass indicator,
- the reflective fixpoint status.
Store these data in a serialisable structure ResidualSnapshot. Implement a collector that builds a sequence of ResidualSnapshots indexed by K (and optionally by N,M). These sequences are the concrete objects on which tightness, correlation with true zeros, and Lyapunov decrease can later be checked.

children.title: Analytic Lift Hooks (Traits)
Flag 6 Orchestrator
children.prompt:
Implement a top-level Flag6Orchestrator that:
1. builds the CNF family,
2. solves it with Cadical,
3. extracts ResidualSnapshots,
4. invokes any registered TightnessCertificate / UniformMourreCertificate / ContinuityOfResidualExtraction / LyapunovFunctional,
5. reports whether the finite SAT part succeeded and whether any analytic certificate is present.

If all required certificates return positive, the orchestrator may print a structured claim that the conditions of Flag 6 are satisfied; otherwise it must clearly state that the infinite lift remains open. Never assert that the Riemann Hypothesis has been proved solely from SAT results.

children.title: Documentation of the CNF / Analytic Boundary
children.prompt:
In the generated crate documentation and in code comments, state explicitly:

- Flag 6 = infinite residual-vanishing + exact pure-point support = the non-trivial zeros of Ξ.
- The CNF family Φ^⋆_{N,M,K} only decides the finite conjunct of Flag 6.
- The remaining conjuncts (tightness, uniform Mourre, continuity of T, Lyapunov) are analytic and live at the level of set theory / analysis.
- A Rust implementation that solves every finite CNF instance has completed the propositional part of Flag 6 but has not captured Flag 6 itself.

This boundary must be visible to any user of the crate.
